messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: GPU telemetry alert — correctable/uncorrectable ECC/Xid events spiking across multiple nodes (gpu-node-17 / gpu-node-22 / gpu-node-23). Observed driver resets, container restarts, and increased OOMs on inference fleet. Paging on-call @Maria O'Neill.

Maria O'Neill: ack — jumping in. collecting logs and live metrics now. linking traces to this thread.

Dave Chen: i'm watching pods and infra metrics. memory-correctable errors rising, kernel resets showing up ~every 30-90s on node-22 and node-23. several inference-worker pods restarted with OOMKill.

Sasha Ilyin: confirmed. pods with heavy KV-cache usage are the ones restarting first. listing nodes: gpu-node-17,gpu-node-22,gpu-node-23.

Maria O'Neill: quick plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain non-critical pods 3) route live traffic to fallback pool 4) escalate infra for driver/firmware check. running commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-22` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

OpsBot: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-22` -> success. Drain started, 12 pods evicted.

Kevin Patel: pasting kernel snippet for visibility:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCIe Bus) 31, PID=0, GPU=0000:65:00.0: Ch 00000000 
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: Xid (PCIe Bus) 47, Rm 0, ChannelID 00000000, Class 0f, subcode 00
[ 1234.569210] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4521 (inference-worker) total-vm:...kB
```

Kevin Patel: first two lines look like driver-issued Xids then immediate OOM on a few pods.

Maria O'Neill: Linh, do we have any open customer jobs in the impacted region? Should we put a banner?

Linh Tran (CS): one active customer job in us-east experiencing degraded latency. I'll open a bridge and post a status page entry. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/3287654321

Dave Chen: attempted quick mitigation: `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm` on gpu-node-22 — yielded short reduction in Xid rate then resets resumed on gpu-node-23. Not a durable fix.

Sasha Ilyin: infra suggests we bring up replacement instances with the last-known-stable driver (nvidia-driver-535.86) and soft-eject the flaky hosts. Avoid immediate mass reboot.

Maria O'Neill: executing soft-eject: cordoned nodes will be marked `soft-eject:true` in cluster metadata so autoscaler avoids reusing the same AMI. Starting node replacement: spin new nodes with driver 535.86; drain and decommission the three suspect hosts. Also enabling fallback routing: `redwood-route set-priority inference=dedicated-fallback` to move incoming inference requests off the impacted pool.

IncidentBot: created incident ticket INC-2026-3287654321 and attached initial logs.

OpsBot: Eviction summary: gpu-node-17 -> 8 pods; gpu-node-22 -> 12 pods; gpu-node-23 -> 10 pods. New nodes spun: gpu-spare-77, gpu-spare-78.

Kevin Patel: after replacement and routing change, Xid spike count dropped to baseline within ~12m. no further container OOMs observed on the new nodes. Monitoring window: 20m no new resets.

Linh Tran (CS): status page updated, affected customers notified via email and in-product banner. No evidence of data corruption; only transient job latency and restarts.

Maria O'Neill: interim mitigation complete: 1) drained and soft-ejected affected hosts 2) launched replacement nodes with rollback driver 3) traffic routed to fallback pool 4) bridge open for customer comms. Latency normalized ~12 minutes after action.

Dave Chen: infra dug into hardware telemetry — ECC correctable counts for the three nodes were rising steadily over last 48h. We're coordinating with cloud provider to run a deeper memory/PCIe diagnostic on the flaky hosts.

Sasha Ilyin: note: KV-cache heavy pods were most impacted; add action to evaluate caching behavior under driver reset scenarios.

Maria O'Neill: post-incident action items (short list):
- Automate soft-eject when Xid rate > threshold for N minutes
- Create a driver-canary pool running candidate drivers for 24h before fleet-wide deploys
- Add telemetry to correlate KV cache sizes / allocation patterns with ECC/Xid events
- Run full ECC scan / health check across fleet and flag hosts with growing counts
- Update runbook with `soft-eject` and fallback-routing commands

Kevin Patel: uploading comprehensive logs to INC-2026-3287654321.

Linh Tran (CS): closing customer comms loop, sharing timeline to affected orgs.

Maria O'Neill: closing pager for now. please add any missed notes to the incident ticket.

OpsBot: Incident closed by Maria O'Neill at 3287654400. :white_check_mark:
